correctness.rationale: For each nonidentity permutation, all five consecutive four-term equations \(E_s=0\) and fifteen valid weak-order/nonnegativity inequalities \(I_j\le0\) on two blocks are explicitly constructed. The 23 included exact rational Farkas identities express the sum of the first block as a nonnegative combination of inequalities modulo equalities, so that nonnegative first block is zero; this forces all later terms to zero. A standard-library validator recomputes all 23 identities coefficientwise with fractions, and separately tests identity-branch examples. The identity case follows from the Padovan recurrence and a direct induction giving precisely \(0\le u\le v\le w\le u+v\). No infinite conclusion is inferred from finite enumeration of terms.

value.rationale: The fixed permutation-block ordering question is explicit in the originating article and its classification through degree three. Classifying the first missing degree four gives a natural complete infinite-sequence theorem with a qualitative phase change: nonzero nonmonotone Fibonacci-derived patterns of length three disappear at length four. The result is not a mere isolated small numerical case: the finite 23-case rational dual computation proves a uniform statement for unbounded sequences, with an exact closed cone of initial triples in the only surviving pattern. It also supplies a finite obstruction mechanism for related rank-controlled local recurrences.
